And as of now, we want to maintain our guidance for the volume as well as our margins

items.statement: Targets 35-40% volume growth over next 9 months to meet FY26 guidance
items.quote: Our aim is to counter pricing pressure through expected reduction in both raw material and other variable costs, as well as fixed cost optimizations and operating leverage by increasing volumes.

items.statement: No new capex planned for FY26
items.quote: No new CAPEX is planned.

items.statement: Domestic MDF volumes degrew 8.5% YoY due to BIS QCOs discontinuing 37,000 CBM commercial-grade sales
items.quote: While sequentially our domestic MDF volumes grew by ~2% versus Quarter 4 FY '25, there was a degrowth of ~8.5% versus Quarter 1 of last year, largely due to the discontinuation of 37,000 cubic meters of commercial-grade MDF sales post-implementation of BIS QCOs.

items.statement: Domestic MDF sales grew 47% like-for-like excluding discontinued commercial-grade segment
items.quote: Excluding this, domestic sales grew by 47% on a like-for-like basis.

items.statement: Exports flat sequentially, down 40% YoY due to geopolitical disruptions
items.quote: Our volumes were almost flat sequentially but de-grew by 40% year-on-year. Obviously, exports has been more of an opportunistic play for us, and we have been taking conscious calls based on possible volumes versus margin play. The recent geo-political situation, especially in the Middle East, also disrupted movements, impacting volume growth.

items.statement: Gross margins improved ~2.5% to 47% due to 7% sequential drop in timber prices
items.quote: Timber prices are on course correction already and were lower by 7% sequentially, leading to an improvement of ~2.5% on gross margins, consolidated gross margins being 47% for Quarter 1.

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 4% (Rs. 13 crore) excluding FX impact on Euro borrowings
items.quote: Consolidated operating EBITDA excluding the impact of currency movement on the euro borrowing for the new plant was Rs. 13 crores or 4% of revenues.

items.statement: Margins impacted by ~3% due to new thin panel plant stabilization costs
items.quote: The second piece was initial stabilization of the new thin panel plant, which Shobhan Ji already talked about, which is what led to a higher consumption, largely on power and fuel. This impacted margins by another ~3% versus the last fiscal.

items.statement: Average scheme discount of 3% offered in July to dealers
items.quote: In July, I think on an average basis, I would say it could be somewhere around about 3-odd percent.

items.statement: Domestic demand robust (low-to-mid double-digit CAGR) but volume growth impacted by peer price/credit aggression and channel inventory liquidation
items.quote: On the domestic front, though demand continues to be robust, growing at a lower-to-mid double-digit CAGR, the recent bunching up of capacity additions led to price and credit aggression by peers to quickly gain relative market share, impacting volume growth.

items.statement: Plywood sales yet to stabilize; revival expected over next few quarters

items.statement: Commercial-grade MDF (discontinued) converted to industrial-grade; majority transitioned in Q1 FY26

So, we have been able to convert those volumes into our industrial grade sales. And not entirely, but the majority of it has already been done so.

items.statement: BIS compliance for MSMEs (effective Aug FY26) to reduce unorganized segment competition

items.statement: Double-digit constant currency growth for FY26 and FY27
items.quote: We are confident that this momentum will help us deliver double-digit growth over a three-year cycle that began last year and will carry through FY '27.

items.statement: EBITDA margin maintained at 20-22% for FY26

items.statement: No MDR/P2M incentive clarity; not factored into financial model
items.quote: As Rishi also highlighted, current lack of clarity around MDR and P2M incentive persist. Should a favourable policy framework be introduced, it has potential to provide a further boost to our margins.

items.statement: FY26 net store additions target 120-130
items.quote: FY '26 onwards, we aspire to open 120 to 130 stores plus net additions going forward, given the lower store closure rates this year.

items.statement: SSSG to reach mid-single-digit in coming quarters
items.quote: We are turning every stone. We are putting an effort in every aspect to make that happen. So I think that is something we, as management will achieve, and we are very positive that we will do it over the next few quarters

items.statement: Gross margin to stay in 62-63.5% range
items.quote: See, I think it will be in that range of 62% to 63%, Gaurav. I think 63% is what we have delivered in Q1. And I think we will be -- we will be in that range between 62% to 63% or 62% to 63.5%, we will be in that range.

items.statement: 60-70% of FY26 store openings in new virgin markets
items.quote: Well, our endeavor is to do at least 60% to 70% of our store openings in new virgin markets.

items.statement: LFS additions in Q1 were 200 stores (10% of current network)
items.quote: See, well, look, we got the right opportunity from our existing channel partners, and we are very thankful to them. So we got the right opportunity, and it was also aligning with those cities where we wanted to also be part of. And luckily, we got those outlets and we've added in Q1.

items.statement: LFS additions in Q2/Q3 to be more stable
items.quote: In Q2 and Q3, I don't foresee too many LFS additions because we've just added a good number of stores. So we are pretty decently penetrated with our existing partners.

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 63% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Our gross margins, which stood at 63%, driven by further easing of raw material costs and a favorable product mix.

items.statement: ASP at INR805 in June 2025 due to shift to value-added products
items.quote: Our ASP stood at INR805 as of June 2025, driven by continued shift towards value-added products.

items.statement: New pants/trousers products priced INR1,000-INR1,200
items.quote: Yes. No, we are trying to keep it very sharply priced. So I think it will range between INR1,000 and INR1,200.

items.statement: Demand recovery expected in upcoming quarters driven by festive season
items.quote: We remain confident in the strength of India's consumption story and expect to see revival in demand in the upcoming quarters, driven by a successful upcoming festive season.

items.statement: SSSG declined 2% in Q1 FY26 due to softer footfalls, supply chain disruptions, and Eid timing
items.quote: SSSG declined by 2%, primarily due to softer footfalls. Additionally, temporary supply chain disruptions from Bangladesh route led to a limited availability of the selected SKUs across some stores.

items.statement: LFS demand marginally negative in June, not yet positive
items.quote: From a June perspective, LFS is marginally negative.

items.statement: LFS business expected to stabilize in coming quarters
items.quote: I think the volatility should be less. I'm quite optimistic that the coming quarters in the LFS business should be good.

items.statement: New categories (women's topwear, select menswear) to launch in 15-20 stores by August 2025
items.quote: We are in the process of rolling out new categories, including women's topwear and select menswear across 15 to 20 stores. The initial launch will begin in the first week of August with a few stores.

items.statement: Supply chain disruptions from Bangladesh had small revenue impact
items.quote: I'm guessing there would be a little impact. I wouldn't say that our revenue growth has got hampered only because of Bangladesh. I wouldn't say that, but I'm sure it would have had a small impact.

items.statement: Inventory days at 98, to be optimized
items.quote: Our inventory days stood at 98 days, at which we are going to further look to optimize.

items.statement: Promoters reduced pledge from ~9.5 lakh to ~48-49 lakh shares (16-17% of holding) in July 2025
items.quote: Currently, the number of see, we had reduced about 9 lakh to 9.5 lakh shares we had released the pledge in the month of July, July end, we just released. So now our pending shares which are pledged are about 48 lakh to 49 lakh shares.

items.statement: FY26 yield guidance of 90 basis points
items.quote: we remain confident in our ability to sustain a yield within the guided range of 90 basis points for the full FY '26.

items.statement: FY26 consolidated operating profit margin guidance of 23-24% (excluding ESOP)
items.quote: we are very comfortable that our full year guidance of 23% to 24% of operating profit margin should remain steady.

items.statement: Employee cost increase of ~20% YoY (including 15-16% fixed salary hike)
items.quote: I think full year cost will increase in line of about 20% to your last year cost, mainly because of 15% to 16% hike in the fixed component, which has happened at the beginning of the year.

items.statement: AUM growth of 8.3% sequentially and 23.4% YoY
items.quote: our AUM continues to scale up sharply, growing 8.3% sequentially and 23.4% year-on-year.

items.statement: Equity AUM grew 13.9% QoQ, driven by mark-to-market gains
items.quote: our equity AUM grew by 13.9%, largely driven by strong mark-to-market gain of INR11,360 crores.

items.statement: SIP book crossed INR1,000 crore milestone in current month
items.quote: our monthly SIP book stood at INR996 crores. And I'm pleased to share you that when I'm talking to you now, I think we already crossed INR1,000 crores milestone in the current month.

items.statement: Yield pressure from SBI/Kotak repricing (~INR2.68 crore FY26 impact)
items.quote: full year impact of Kotak's repricing would be in the regi on of INR2.68 crores

items.statement: SBI/Kotak repricing impact partially offset by new business mix shift
items.quote: we are able to pass on the sharing percentage to the distribution. So in terms of margin percentage yield, there is no impact on our books.

items.statement: Insurance fresh premium grew 21% YoY (general insurance +50% YoY)
items.quote: Fresh premium on insurance side rose by 21% Y-o-Y, led by general insurance, where our focus is largely on health. This environment has been exceptional. Fresh general insurance business grew by almost more than 50% Y -o-Y

items.statement: Shift from traditional life insurance (40-45% of book) to newer products (TULIP, ULIP)
items.quote: plan computes around 40%, 45%. And within that, the guaranteed plans around 30%, 35%. So practically, yes, you can say that the main reason is the reduction in the business from guaranteed plan

items.statement: Competitive pressure on distributor payouts (some players at 85-90%)
items.quote: a few of them were private equity packed have made it more competitive in terms of paying the commercial and then they go up to 85%, 90

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 25-26% (consolidated)
items.quote: we continue to maintain our EBITDA guidance of 25% to 26%. So, we are not c hanging the guidance either for the GC or EBITDA

items.statement: FY26 gross margin guidance maintained above 70%
items.quote: we have maintained the guidance that our gross margins will be upward of 70% and even in this quarter as well, it is upward of 70%.

items.statement: FY26 capex guidance maintained at 5% of revenue
items.quote: The CAPEX as a percentage of revenue is 3.6%, which is lower than our guidance of 5% of revenue for FY'26.

items.statement: FY26 BSV topline growth guidance maintained at 18-20%
items.quote: So, for BSV, we are maintaining guidance. So, sales growth of 18%-20% with margins tad higher of 26%-28%.

items.statement: FY26 tax rate guidance maintained at 20-21% (effective tax rate)
items.quote: So, we would like to maintain 20% to 21% guidance from the ETR.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 capex spend at Rs. 127 crores (3.6% of revenue)
items.quote: Our CAPEX spend during the quarter has increased moderately to Rs. 127 crores in Q1 FY'26 as compared to Rs. 125 crores in Q1 FY'25.

items.statement: FY26 biosimilar facility estimated cash outflow at Rs. 100 crores
items.quote: So, in FY26, the estimated cash outflow will be close to Rs 100 crores for this facility.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 domestic revenue grew 19% YoY (organic growth 10% YoY)
items.quote: Our domestic business revenue in Q1 FY’26 registered a healthy growth of 19% year-on-year, driven by organic growth for the quarter of 10% year-on-year.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 international revenue grew 81% YoY (organic growth single-digit)
items.quote: Our revenue from international business increased to Rs. 469 crore in Q1 FY'26, up by 81% year-on-year from Rs. 259 crore in Q1 FY'25, with single-digit organic growth.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 OTC revenue grew 15% YoY to Rs. 237 crores
items.quote: During the quarter, revenue from OTC business increased by 15% year-on-year to Rs. 237 crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 modern trade/e-commerce channel share increased to 11% (50% YoY growth)
items.quote: The modern trade and e-commerce channel registered a growth of about 50% year-on-year, resulting its share to increase to 11%, from 9% in Q1 FY'25.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 BSV Rx business shows high double-digit growth (secondary sales)
items.quote: In the India business, there were two parts. So, Rx business, we took a big corrective action in Q4. Sales were hardly anything. And in Q1, we have started to see very strong growth. You can see some data from secondary IQ VIA. It is a high double-digit growth.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 BSV specialty business shows strong Q-o-Q growth (FSH, Humog, ASVS)
items.quote: So, the fertility business, if you see FSH, our Foligraf secondary growth is 35%. If you see Humog, Hucog all are growing 10% plus. ASVS, which is the anti-snake venom is also showing high double-digit growth.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 gross margin declined 130 bps YoY to 70.5% (due to sales mix and inventory accruals)
items.quote: Our gross margins for the quarter declined by 130 basis point year-on-year basis to 70.5% from 71.8% in Q1 FY'25, which is due to unfavorable sales mix and certain inventory-related accruals taken in the current quarter.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin increased 20 bps YoY to 23.8% (adjusted EBITDA margin down 120 bps YoY)
items.quote: The reported EBITDA margin for the quarter is at 23.8%, which has increased by 20 basis point on year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 OTC EBITDA margin declined 2% (due to sales mix shift)
items.quote: Rajeev Juneja: I mean, Siddharth, don't go by one quarter. We always talk about the annual growth. Whatever projections have been given would be achieved. And the 1st Quarter, the first half is always a bit more aggressive as far as the spending is concerned. So, naturally, you see that EBITDA margin has gone down.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 chronic therapy sales grew 14.7% YoY (1.1x IPM outperformance)
items.quote: Our secondary sales increased 9.2% year-on-year as compared to 8.6% IPM growth, led by 2.5% growth in sales volume and 14.7% growth in chronic therapy, indicating an overall outperformance of 1.1x of IPM.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 acute therapies (anti-infectives, respiratory) outperform IPM by 1.5x
items.quote: Our key acute therapies like anti -infectives and respiratory out perform IPM by over 1.5 x, and our chronic therapies continue to deliver an outperformance in this quarter as well

items.statement: Q1 FY26 chronic therapies outperform IPM (1.5x cardiology, 1.6x anti-diabetes)
items.quote: our chronic therapies continue to deliver an outperformance in this quarter as well, led by 1.5 x in cardiology and 1.6x in anti-diabetes

items.statement: Q1 FY26 volume growth to IPM at 1.8x (led by anti-infectives, respiratory)
items.quote: we are seeing encouraging trends with 1.8 x volume growth to IPM, led by outperformance in anti -infectives and respiratory segments

items.statement: Q1 FY26 chronic share (ex-BSV) increased 190 bps YoY to 38.8% (1.4x IPM chronic growth)
items.quote: Our chronic share, excluding BSV, increased by 190 bps year-on-year to 38.8% in Q1 FY'26, as compared to 36.9% in Q1 FY'25, driven by an outperformance of 1.4x to IPM chronic growth.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 Panacea portfolio growing at 25%+ YoY
items.quote: Panacea is growing 25% plus kind of a growth. It is in line with our commentary we gave last time.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 BSV international business growing mid-teens
items.quote: international business continue to be at mid-teen kind of growth.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 BSV Rx business shows nominal YoY growth (high double-digit Q-o-Q)
items.quote: Also, on the specialty side, we are seeing good traction. We had small changes, leadership changes, and we have started to see good Q -on-Q growth. In the next quarter onwards, I think we start seeing good YOY growth also. There is some YOY growth, but it is nomin al at the

items.statement: Q1 FY26 gross margin headwind from inventory accruals (slow-moving items) and sales mix
items.quote: Ashutosh Dhawan: Somehow, it is echoing. So, I understand there is a drop in the gross margin of 1.3% year-on-year basis and 1.1% is on a Q-on-Q basis. So, inventory-related accrual is forming part of this.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 BSV Rx business shows flattish YoY growth (corrective actions taken)
items.quote: Your observation is right. So, it is a flattish kind of growth on an overall basis. But because we have taken some corrective actions, and if you see BSV past trends of last 2-3 years, it is more skewed towards second half.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 Gynae segment shows slowed growth (Dydrogesterone, Dydroboon impact)
items.quote: So, Siddharth, answering your first question, yes, your observation is correct that we have slowed down a bit in Gynae, but t he major impact has come from Dy drogesterone and dydroboon mostly

items.statement: FY26 debt repayment of Rs. 2,000 crores (Rs. 500 crores paid in Q1, Rs. 1,500 crores targeted in October 2025)
items.quote: for the acquisition-related debt repayment, we have scheduled Rs. 2,000 crores to be paid in FY'26, out of which Rs. 500 crores has been paid in Q1 and the balance Rs. 1,500 crores, we are targeting to pay in October 2025.

items.statement: FY26 interest cost for acquisition debt estimated at Rs. 450-475 crores
items.quote: And the total interest cost towards this acquisition debt for this year would be in the range of Rs. 450 crores - Rs. 475 crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 net debt reduced to Rs. 5,249 crores (net debt to EBITDA ratio improved to 1.6x)
items.quote: have reduced our net debt position to Rs. 5,249 crores as of 30th June 25, resulting in further improving our net debt to EBITDA ratio to 1.6x in Q1 FY'26 on trailing 12-month basis

items.statement: Q1 FY26 cash EPS increased slightly to Rs. 15.9 (from Rs. 15.8)
items.quote: During the quarter, cash EPS, which is EPS adjusted for non-cash items like depreciation and amortization, has slightly increased to Rs. 15.9 from Rs 15.8 in Q1 FY'25.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 R&D expenses at Rs. 79 crores (2.2% of sales, up from 1.7% in Q1 FY25)
items.quote: The R&D expenses for the quarter was Rs. 79 crores, which remains at 2.2% of sales and is higher than R&D spend of 1.7% of sales as incurred during Q1 FY'25.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 depreciation and amortization expenses increased to Rs. 219 crores (up from Rs. 103 crores in Q1 FY25)
items.quote: In Q1 FY'26, the depreciation and amortization expenses have increased to Rs. 219 crores as compared to Rs. 103 crores in Q1 FY'25.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 net profit declined 17.4% YoY to Rs. 445 crores (due to higher finance costs, depreciation, and BSV consolidation)
items.quote: The profit after tax for Q1 FY'26 has decreased by 17.4% year-on-year to Rs. 445 crores, on account of higher finance costs and depreciation costs pursuant to BSV consolidation.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 net operating working capital days reduced to 48 (from 50 in Q4 FY25)
items.quote: The net operating working capital days for the quarter on trailing 12-month basis have decreased to 48 days as compared to 50 days in Q4 FY'25.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 cash flow from operations increased 54% YoY to Rs. 840 crores (due to BSV consolidation and working capital improvement)
items.quote: The cash flow from operations has increased to Rs. 840 crores as compared to Rs. 546 crores in Q1 FY'25, which is on a year-on-year basis an increase of 54%. This is primarily on account of consolidation of BSV operating cash flows and improvement in working capital.

items.statement: EBITDA margins preserved, PAT margins lower due to higher depreciation and finance costs
items.quote: The EBITDA margins are likely to be preserved, but the gap between PAT and EBITDA is expected to widen, leading to lower PAT margins this year.

items.statement: Dombivli capex ~INR200 crores spent, another ~INR200 crores needed to start operations
items.quote: we have incurred something around INR200 crores of expenditure already till now, and we should incur similar, around INR200 crores more, in the next few months till we start the Dombivli hospital.

items.statement: Dombivli Phase 1 capex ~INR400 crores, Phase 2 <INR100 crores
items.quote: So we would spend a little over INR400 crores for Phase 1 and less than INR100 crores for Phase 2.

items.statement: Pune hospital capex ~15% of total in FY27
items.quote: Pune will just spend about 15% in the next year.

items.statement: Solar plant capex ~INR5 crores, annual savings ~INR1 crore
items.quote: Indore solar plant has cost us about roughly INR5 crores in capex. It is expected to result in around INR1 crore in opex savings annually.

items.statement: Patient volume grew 11.7% YoY to ~2.6 lakhs in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The overall patient volume also has increased by 11.7% to 2.6-odd lakhs in the first quarter of this year.

items.statement: Insurance payor mix increasing YoY, trend to continue
items.quote: The insurance penetration is increasing year-on-year everywhere in the country, and that will get reflected in the patients who walk into our facilities also.

items.statement: Pune and Indore occupancy to peak at mid-70% range
items.quote: So all the hospitals, we expect the peak to be in the mid-70% range.

items.statement: Dombivli EBITDA breakeven expected by Year 2
items.quote: current thought is by year 2, we should breakeven on an EBITDA level.

items.statement: Dombivli EBITDA burn ~INR2-2.5 cr/month in early operations
items.quote: the experience has been around INR2 crores, INR2.5 crores a month. I think we should be similar.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth expected to improve with deal pipeline strengthening and Tectonic progress
items.quote: FY '25 was a somewhat challenging year for Indegene as we had some unexpected client issues, but those look like largely behind us now. Looking at FY '26, our deal pipeline has improved, and we are seeing the results in our improved deal booking data.

items.statement: Investing in AI/Gen AI tools and platforms for Tectonic and broader solutions
items.quote: we continue to double down on that. Operationally, we have done a strategic reorg of our sales function and completed a remapping exercise to drive higher effectiveness and traction and efficiency. We're adding senior leaders to strengthen and drive growth in our sales functions, consulting and capabilities like data analytics, content and medical affairs and regulatory

items.statement: Pipeline growth strong with clients returning for next-level program evolution
items.quote: This was a good quarter in terms of new pipeline growth, which also alludes -- referring back to my earlier conversation of clients coming back to the table, thinking about their programs.

items.statement: 2 large deal wins (>USD 3M ACV) expected to go live in Q2 FY26
items.quote: We also maintained our momentum on deal wins with 2 large deal wins of 3 million plus ACV. One in ECS expected to go live in Q2 itself and the other in brand activation to go live in

items.statement: Tectonic revenue from 2 customers; 3 more in advanced conversations
items.quote: Revenues from 2 customers, in advanced stages of conversations with 3 more.

items.quote: The EBITDA margin for the quarter was stable at 20.2%. And we have spoken about Tectonic and our continued investments in Tectonic, including certain unpaid POCs at this point in time. And at normal rates of charge out, this would have added about 0.3% to our margin.

items.statement: Top 20 clients stable (76.2% revenue share); accounts beyond top 20 growing 5% QoQ
items.quote: Top 20 is business as usual and contributed 76.2% of revenues. Accounts beyond the top 20 continue to have higher growth, growing by 5% quarter-on-quarter in Q1.

items.statement: Tectonic unlocks 35–50% of marketing budgets (vs. prior 5–15%)
items.quote: With Tectonic, we believe that, that 5% to 15% increases to 35% to 50 -ish depending on the customer and the situation from a budget perspective

items.statement: EBITDA guidance for FY26

items.statement: EBITDA margin expansion
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 25.4%, and which also has an expansion of over 700 basis points

items.statement: Input cost trend (China)
items.quote: we are now seeing an upward trend that will, over a period of time, have an impact on our numbers

items.statement: Price revision plan for input cost pass-through

items.statement: US demand outlook
items.quote: the demand outlook both in India and U.S. remains secular and long-term in nature

items.statement: Order book of 25 GW (~$5.5-6 billion)
items.quote: Our order book is actually 25 gigawatts, which is equivalent to INR49,000 crores which is equal to what, roughly $4 billion about $6 billion roughly of order book.

items.statement: EPC order book pipeline of 25+ GW (domestic + overseas)
items.quote: we have -- I did in the call of our EPC arm Waaree Renewable Technologies that the pipeline for EPC business is 25-gigawatt plus.

items.statement: Total capex of INR15,000 crores over next 2 years
items.quote: our total capex including everything, the recent expansion of 4 gigawatts including our 6 gigawatt integrated facility and the other adjacent businesses like battery and all. The total capex is about INR15,000 crores.

items.statement: Capex for 1 GW cell capacity: INR750-800 crores

items.quote: at this point in time, across the US about 2.2% of overall power consumed is used for data centers associated with artificial intelligence... By 2030, that number is set to grow to 7.5% to 8%.

items.statement: Module EBITDA margins target: 17-18%; cell margins target: 21-22% (up 300-400 bps)
items.quote: we should look at around 18% kind of margins on the EBITDA side and 17% to 18%. And with the cell we expect it to go up by 300 to 400 basis points

items.statement: US ADD investigation impact minimal due to global footprint and transparency
items.quote: we should be in a position because of our global footprint and because of the fact that we are a publicly listed company, we will be in a position to defend our case well with minimal impact

items.statement: US 25% tariffs: mixed contract clauses for pass-through; gross margin focus
items.quote: it is going to be a mixed bag. But net-net, like I said, we will always make sure that we are driving towards a gross margin, which leads to an EBITDA that we have committed to our investors

items.statement: Contribution margin improvement trajectory continues; expect higher margin improvement in current quarter
items.quote: we actually expect to make an even higher contribution margin improvement in the current quarter. So, all of this improvement is not back ended.

items.statement: Contribution margin expected to reach neutrality between Dec and June quarter of calendar year 2026
items.quote: our guidance remains that we expect to get to contribution margin neutrality between December and June quarter of calendar year 2026.

items.quote: This is more of a one-time, say effort and the significant movement that we have been able to make. And over time, this will mean that we will go back to more category margins

items.statement: Heightened competitive intensity remains, with new players entering the market
items.quote: at an absolute level the intensity in the market, we see it being at the heightened level. There are new players also entering the market.

items.statement: Flexibility to invest for growth in subsequent quarters due to heightened marketing investments

items.statement: Quick commerce contribution margin breakeven timeline maintained

items.statement: Channel inventory higher than normal due to subdued summer demand
items.quote: Given that until the March’25 quarter we were placing inventory very aggressively with the channel, the channel-end inventory at this point in time is higher than what we expect at the end of the summer quarter.

items.statement: Channel inventory normalization expected only with next summer sales
items.quote: The channel inventory will only sort of get normalized once tertiary sales begins. And closer to next summer, sales will begin and channel inventory will get normalized.

items.statement: Non-air cooler categories (tower fans, kitchen cooling fans, industrial coolers, water heaters) grew ~50%+ CAGR over last 3-4 years; now ~25% of revenue

items.statement: Non-air cooler categories grew similarly YoY despite subdued summer
items.quote: These categories, even within this financial year, they have grown by a similar rate versus last year. So in that sense, these are giving us all and contra-seasonal portfolio to continue to build on.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 revenue decline entirely due to weak summer; no structural or competitive issues
items.quote: The loss of sales is entirely on account of a weak summer because the same has been experienced by all products and by all industries in summer categories like air conditioners, fans, coolers, refrigerators and everything associated with it.

items.statement: South India saw worst degrowth; uniform decline across other regions

items.statement: Air cooler demand more spontaneous than air conditioners, leading to higher degrowth

items.statement: US exports grew significantly YoY; retail chains shortlisting models for upcoming summer

items.statement: Exports expected to replicate or improve upon last year’s performance

items.statement: LSV (Large Space Ventilated) margin profile significantly better than air coolers

items.statement: US tariffs evolving but not impacting plans; India’s tariffs remain lower than China’s

items.quote: In Q1 FY '26, we have incurred capital expenditure of approximately INR13 crores, and we are committed to our plan of approximately INR100 crores of capex over 2 years.

items.statement: PCMB business order-driven, 60% capacity utilization expected by Q3 FY26
items.quote: We expect to get to about 60% utilization by Q3 -- from Q3 onwards in the PCMB business.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin of 16%, improved by 237 bps QoQ
items.quote: Our EBITDA increased by 19% Q-o-Q basis to INR21 crores and margin stood strong at 16% and improved by 237 basis points on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improvement sustainable, driven by raw material cost reduction and operational efficiency
items.quote: in our overall margins has happened right from the gross margin level, where we have seen a 300 bps plus improvement. And we believe at this stage, it seems sustainable. I don't see any reason for that to change

items.statement: RCB plant EBITDA margin expected at 15-16%
items.quote: In terms of margins achievable, we expect to operate at around 15% to 16% EBITDA margin, very similar to our existing material recycling facilities.

items.statement: 10-15% cost savings from increased tire feedstock optionality
items.quote: With increased optionality on using different types of tires as feedstock, we expect cost savings of 10% to 15%.

items.statement: Consumer segment demand to revive in Q2 FY26 post seasonal shift
items.quote: Consumer segment demand is expected to revive in the upcoming quarters following a seasonal shift influenced by early monsoon.

items.statement: PCMB business top-line contribution of INR30-35 crores in FY26
items.quote: We are expecting approximately INR30 crores to INR35 crores of contribution in our overall top line from the PCMB business.

items.statement: RCB plant top-line contribution of INR70+ crores at full capacity
items.quote: We expect approximately in full capacity utilization, probably around INR70-odd crores a year.

items.statement: Oman ELT prices increased due to new recycling facilities
items.quote: In Oman, subsequent to us making our investment, we have seen at least three new recycling facilities have also come up. As a result, the price of end-of-life tires there has gone up, putting some pressure on margins for the time being.

items.statement: Domestic ELT procurement expected to increase to 40% in 2-3 years from current 30%
items.quote: Maybe after 2, 3 years, it could become 60-40 possibly in favor of domestic.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 capex achieved INR202.5 cr, FY26 capex budget remains INR860 cr
items.quote: Capex achieved in Q1 is INR202.5 crores, and our Capex budget for this financial year remains intact at INR860 crores.

items.statement: EXIM originating volume Q1 FY26: 531,099 TEUs; domestic: 121,624 TEUs
items.quote: I will tell you. Originating volume for EXIM 5,31,099, Domestic 1,21,624. Total 6,52,723.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EXIM growth maintained at 10.2% YoY
items.quote: And for Q2, I can tell you same growth is being maintained. So what is your question exactly? I'm not able to understand. We are able to maintain that growth and we are -- there is a demand in import, export both.

items.statement: Rail freight margin Q1 FY26: 26.96% (up from 24.36% Q1 FY25)
items.quote: Rail freight margin increased from 24.36% to 26.96%. Operating margin increased from 28.58% to 29.81%.

items.statement: Empty running cost decreased 13.7% YoY, improving bottom line
items.quote: There has been substantial decline in empty running of flats as well as empty containers, both in domestic and EXIM. Total empty running cost decrease was 13.7%, and which has contributed in a positive manner to our bottom line.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 domestic demand robust, especially Eastern India (Gunny Bales Traffic) and Gujarat (Morbi, Rafaleshwar)
items.quote: In domestic, after a muted Q1, now there is a very robust growth we are observing in Q2 with excellent demand from Eastern India, mainly Gunny Bales Traffic, then our new terminal at Morbi, Rafaleshwar in Gujarat also will give boost in business.

items.statement: EXIM demand strong, 12% growth in imports (Mundra +8.4%, JNPT +19.3%, Chennai +19.4%, Vizag +29%)
items.quote: Overall, there has been a 12% growth in imports in this quarter. Mundra saw a growth of 8.4%; JNPT 19.3%; and Chennai, 19.4%; Vizag port, 29%. So there is a very good growth in imports that we have observed in this quarter.

items.statement: Bulk cement demand enormous (14-15M tonnes/year), rail share <10%; growth expected post-monsoon (Q3 FY26)
items.quote: Demand is enormous. Like we do around 14 to 15 million tonnes in domestic every year. So demand is -- only bulk cement in tank containers can add same volume every year. So hardly 9% to 10% is moving by rail.

items.statement: North India ICD demand (Ludhiana, Tughlakabad, SIDCUL) subdued in Q1 FY26, normalized in Q2
items.quote: The basic reason for this is less demand in North India. North India ICDs, there was less demand of imports, exports like Ludhiana, Tughlakabad and SIDCUL ICDs. So we saw below performance in these ICDs in Q1.

items.statement: EXIM exports growth: auto parts +22%, rice +12%, RMG +14%; imports: aluminum scrap +8%, stainless steel +17%
items.quote: Exports growth has been good in auto parts, 22% growth. Rice saw 12% growth, and ready-made garments, 14% growth. Imports, there was a good growth in aluminum scrap, 8%; stainless steel, 17% growth.

items.statement: Domestic demand to improve post-monsoon (Q3 FY26) with bulk cement, liquid cargo (caustic soda, benzene), and corporate tie-ups (Tata, Jindal, Vedanta, JK Cement)
items.quote: So I think these 2, 3 initiatives like bulk cement and liquid cargo and the association with the top growth, and 40 feet open top containers for steel movement. I think these combined together, we are going to get a good traffic in the domestic.

items.statement: No impact on volumes from global tariffs observed so far; optimistic about alternative trade opportunities
items.quote: Till now, we have not experienced any effect on our volumes as a result of tariffs. But we should be very optimistic. I can only say that if one door is closed, there are several other doors which can be opened.

items.statement: Domestic market share drop (57.7% to 55%) due to avoiding low-margin traffic and competition from PCTO
items.quote: Domestic, actually, we saw a drop in our market share, which was a very big drop. And the reason, as I told in my opening remarks, that low-margin traffic consciously, we have not picked up in domestic.

items.statement: Double stack rakes grew 11.2% YoY (1,505 vs. 1,353 in Q1 FY25); 5 high-speed rakes commissioned, 1,500 containers procured for domestic use
items.quote: We saw a very handsome increase in double stack rakes, 11.2%. We have done 1,505 rakes this quarter, as compared to 1,353 rakes in last year same quarter. We are continuously increasing our infrastructure.

items.statement: First-mile/last-mile services account for ~35% of total volume (INR98 cr revenue in Q1 FY26), used as marketing tool
items.quote: First mile last mile, we are able to do a total volume, around 35%, we are able to do first mile last mile. In Q1 also, we are able to do 35%. Now we are going to scale up.

items.statement: MOU signed with RHS Group (Dubai) for end-to-end logistics (India to UAE); expansion planned to Singapore
items.quote: We signed an MOU with the RHS Group of Dubai for end-to-end logistics solution. And the containers of CONCOR are now moving across the shores of India. Till now, we were giving service only up to our ports, but now they have crossed the ports and they are reaching Dubai.

items.statement: 30% AUM growth for FY26 and next 3 years
items.quote: we are going to remain on course for the 30% growth, and that we believe that is quite healthy growth. We don't think we are going to exceed that this year.

items.statement: AUM to reach ₹50,000 crores by FY28
items.quote: we are quite confident to achieve the 30% growth for the next 3 years by targeting the AUM to be INR50,000 crores by FY 2028

items.statement: ROAA to improve to 4% by FY27
items.quote: Next year onwards, our strong fee income and coupled with our cost-income ratio further coming down because now operating leverage with scale will kick-in. So then our ROAA will improve to about 4%

items.statement: ROAE to reach 16-17% by FY27
items.quote: ROAE will be in the range about 16% to 17%

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio to stabilize at 50% in FY26
items.quote: cost-to-income ratio should remain in the range of about 50% for the year

items.statement: Credit cost to remain below 70 basis points in FY26
items.quote: we don't see that much elevation at the most credit cost will not go beyond 70 basis

items.statement: Co-lending AUM to be 18-20% of total AUM
items.quote: Co-lending AUM, we intend to project in the range of anything between 18% to 20% range

items.statement: Cost of funds to reduce by 30-40 basis points in FY26
items.quote: we should be able to get the benefit of the MCLR reduction by 30 to 40 basis

items.statement: Gross NPA to stay below 2%
items.quote: our GNPA will not cross more than 2%. Our net NPA will not cross more than 1.2

items.quote: Last quarter, we spent about INR26 crores on various initiatives of the technology, data science

items.quote: gold should be in the range of about 37% to 40% kind

items.statement: Housing loans AUM to be 20-22% of total AUM

items.statement: Construction finance AUM to be 17-18% of total AUM
items.quote: Construction finance will remain in the range of about 17%-18%

items.statement: MSME delinquencies rising in Madhya Pradesh; cautious disbursements
items.quote: we have seen some slippage, more particularly from a state of Madhya Pradesh, where we are already turning down our disbursements and we are progressing cautiously on that

items.quote: delinquency has risen in Micro LAP segment. However, we are creating a differentiation by using the technology and data science capability, where various risk triggers are being built

items.statement: India volume growth high single-digit base case, double-digit in some quarters; 25% revenue growth FY26; high single-digit EBITDA growth FY26
items.quote: base case, we will strive to deliver double -digit volume growth in some quarters. Supported by pricing growth, we will target around 25% revenue growth this year. items.statement: Double-digit EBITDA growth CAGR over next two years
items.quote: We are fairly confident of delivering double-digit profit CAGR over the next two years.

items.statement: Revenue ₹15,000 crore in next two years; ₹20,000 crore in next five years
items.quote: There is a very fair chance that we could touch ₹15,000 Crores over the next two years. Therefore, we also believe that the ₹10,000 Crores to ₹20,000 Crores leap can be achieved within the next five years if we continue to maintain this momentum.

items.statement: Digital-first portfolio ARR to reach 2.5x of FY24 by FY27; double-digit EBITDA margins by FY27
items.quote: Given this trajectory, we are on track to reach 2.5x of FY24 ARR by FY27. We continue to operate with a keen eye on the profitability and are striving to deliver double-digit EBITDA margins in this portfolio by FY27.

items.statement: Foods business to deliver 25%+ revenue growth FY26
items.quote: We remain on track to deliver over 25% growth this year and over the medium-term, while steadily improving profitability.

items.statement: VAHO to deliver double-digit volume growth FY26
items.quote: We are confident of maintaining a double-digit growth momentum in the franchise throughout the year.

items.statement: Saffola oil to deliver mid-single-digit volume growth FY26
items.quote: Saffola oil has bounced back to deliver mid-single digit volume growth, which is in line with our medium-term aspiration. We expect the brand to be steady on a full year base.

items.statement: India demand trends stable to improving; premium categories outperform mass segments; alternate channels (Modern Trade, E-commerce, Quick Commerce) lead growth
items.quote: During the quarter, we witnessed stable to improving demand trends in India across urban and rural. Premium categories continued to outperform the mass segments, while alternate channels like Modern Trade, E-commerce and especially Quick Commerce continued to lead growth.

items.statement: India volume growth nearing double-digits; 99% of business gaining or sustaining market share
items.quote: We have continued to deliver a sequential uptick in underlying volume growth in India, which is nearing double-digits, backed by improving traction in the core aided by GT improvement and sustained momentum in our new businesses. Offtake trends have remained encouraging, with nearly the entire business either sustaining or gaining market share.

items.statement: Parachute volume growth minimal despite 60%+ price increase; market share gains in Modern Trade and E-commerce
items.quote: Parachute has continued to demonstrate resilience amidst the hyperinflationary conditions in copra prices. items.statement: Shift to mid/premium segments in VAHO; focus on equity-building over BTL-driven strategies
items.quote: We are confident of maintaining a double -digit growth momentum in the franchise throughout the year on the back of sharper brand activations supported by a strategic pivot from trade-led investments toward s brand-building and therefore increasing SOV, especially in the mid and premium segments

items.statement: Copra inflation due to supply-demand gap (9% drop in crop yield, speculative activities, delayed conversion due to unseasonal rains)
items.quote: The unprecedented levels of inflation in this particular cycle has been due to the supply-demand gap created by a combination of drop in crop yields due to an uneven weather pattern in the first half of 2024 and speculative activities. Further, some unseasonal rains in April and May, and the temperature fluctuation this year, further extended this cycle and led to a sharp spike in April period.

items.statement: Copra price volatility managed via supply chain control and demand rationing
items.quote: We are now in a state where we believe we have much more control of the situation. Because, as you know that copra and the overall coconut demand titration happens in these kinds of inflation, the normal supply & demand imbalance adjusted itself because every consumption point gets titrated. And given our supply chain and other advantages, along with our position building, I think we are in a far

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance for FY26 revised downward to 7% to 9% due to weaker consumer sentiment, especially in the U.S.
items.quote: given the current macro environment, especially the consumer sentiment that we see in U.S., so we are revising the guidance to 7% to 9% for current financial year.

items.statement: Mid-teens revenue growth projected for FY27 and beyond, assuming macroeconomic stabilization.
items.quote: For the periods further ahead, we continue to project mid-teens revenue growth, supported by strong operating leverage and our investment into digital marketing.

items.statement: Capex for FY26 expected to be INR 300-500 million, primarily for software upgrades and routine tangible asset investments.

items.quote: FY '27 may be slightly higher as we are consolidating our UK operation in one place. So around 2 million, 3 million higher in FY '27. So we expect 5 million to 7 million capex overall in the business.

items.statement: Gross margin in Germany improved from 63% to 68%, contributing to EBITDA profitability expectations.
items.quote: gross margin improvement is double digit and higher, while revenue is 7.2% you see, but gross margin is much higher in Germany now onwards.

items.statement: Gross margin held steady at 63.8% in Q1 FY26, within target range of 60%+.
items.quote: Our gross margin held steady at 63.8%, which is reassuring given the macro volatilities.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved by 50 bps YoY to 9.2% in Q1 FY26 due to cost efficiencies.

items.statement: Margin guidance of 60%+ expected to sustain despite U.S. tariff challenges.

items.statement: U.S. tariff of 25% (on top of existing tariffs) will increase costs, but pre-shipped inventory will cushion impact.

items.statement: U.S. demand weakened due to consumer sentiment decline, job market softness, and geopolitical tensions.
items.quote: we are seeing lipstick effect already in U.S. What do I mean by that? The lower price point, slouchy jewellery is selling more right now.

items.statement: Lab-grown diamond jewelry sales grew to 11% of total sales in Q1 FY26 (up from 1% YoY).
items.quote: lab-grown diamond jewellery portfolio, which contributes to 11% of group's overall sales in Q1, up from 1% in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Digital sales now 43% of B2C revenue, targeting 50% by FY27.
items.quote: digital now contributes to 43% of our B2C sales. We now remain on track to reach a 50% digital revenue share by FY '27.

items.statement: U.S. tariffs and weaker consumer sentiment pose near-term challenges, but long-term growth potential remains.
items.quote: Current macroeconomic environment and recent tariff development presents near-term challenge, especially in consumer sentiments. In light of this, we are taking a cautious approach.

items.quote: Consolidated revenue came in at 49,463 Crores just under 49,500 Crores. This was impacted by a decline in the B2B segment. As I had mentioned earlier, this is in line with our guidance, which I gave earlier to peel off ou r low margin revenue in B2B

items.quote: "Constant currency revenue growth continues to remain strong at 6.7% sequentially and this was also helped by a favorable currency movement, which led to a solid reported revenue growth of 6.2% sequentially."

items.statement: Submarine cable capacity expansion: 45 Tbps to 180 Tbps (₹2,000 Cr invested over 5 years)
items.quote: "We have invested over 2000 Crores over the last five years and we expect a further light up from 45 Tbps capacity to 180 Tbps capacity."

items.quote: the margins are under pr essure and the margins are low, i t is a trading business and we have exited the very low margin business in this area, but the rest of the business has a better margin profile but it is really riding on our existing networks and the headwinds that you face here are the shift away from SMS to OTT platforms or in app notifications or even just rate pressures

items.quote: "In the market that we are playing in and the services that we are offering, we estimate that this market could well be in the ballpark of 60,000 Crores."
